global_organization_chain: Summary: preview the actor, forecasting-to-decision interface and conditional outcome (p1).
Introduction: define the past-only four-part commission-bounded task and show a two-module workflow (pp3-4).
Assumptions and notation: name temporal inputs and explanatory component symbols (p5).
Model selection: show lag or interpretability tensions, then introduce Prophet components (pp5-8).
Model repair: locate a pointwise fit concern and insert X-Prophet/XGBoost before decision output (pp9-10).
Decision and implementation: pass forecasts to SMA and adaptive history window, then define reproducible daily steps (pp10-11).
Data and tests: describe normalization, time-series stability and randomness before interpreting predictions (pp11-13).
Prediction results: contrast dated single-step forecasts with the rolling global trace (pp13-15).
Portfolio result: read the reported allocation and end amount from its plotted comparison (p16).
Optimality evidence and asset bookkeeping: move from reported comparisons to fee-aware state updates and a bounded risk interpretation (pp16-19).
Fee sensitivity: vary each cost over the stated range and read the response from Figure 12 (pp19-20).
Strengths, limits and conclusion: return to the two-module claim with source-described constraints (pp20-21).
Trader memo: translate the route, reported allocation and conditional caveat into the required recipient artifact (p22).
Code appendix: corroborate implementation actions without treating code labels as authored prose (pp23-24).

warnings.warning: Equations (20)-(22) and the paragraph beside them number the loss and the final output differently. The skill must keep both numberings and must not pick one to make the derivation read cleanly.

Equation (2) prints a prime on z(t) and a transpose on the same vector. Equation (13) has a bare multiplication sign and no visible k_i. Neither glyph is repaired; a copied formula would invent a coefficient the page does not show.

Algorithm 1 sets MoneyForGold or MoneyForBitcoin to 0 and the next line spends that sleeve. Read literally the buy quantity is zero. Also unresolved: whether the 'most recent trading day' gold price is known at decision time, and whether fractional holdings are allowed. The ledger cannot be executed as printed.

Min-Max uses X_max and X_min with no statement of whether the extremes come from the full series or from data available on that decision day. Full-series extremes leak future prices into today's forecast. No inverse transform is given, so a normalized forecast is not a dollar price. The denominator is undefined when X_max equals X_min.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: Figure 6 caption: most p-values are significantly less than 0.05, so the sequences are not pure random and this is evidence for the following prediction.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: The gold panel starts above 0.05, the axes name no test, and the prose's Q and LB statistics are not on the figure. A falling p-value curve does not establish out-of-sample forecast accuracy. Figure 5's caption calls the same series 'relatively stable' while both price panels trend upward, and no unit-root statistic is printed.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: Figure 9 is captioned as the final prediction using the X-Prophet model, while both panel titles say 'Pridicted with Prophet'.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: Title and caption name different models, 'Predicted' is misspelled in both titles, and neither panel shows an interval or an error. The skill must not describe this figure as measured X-Prophet accuracy. The same gap covers the prose claim that the sliding window 'significantly outperforms' full-window models: Figure 8 shows only that a bracket moves, with no metric.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: One paragraph says bitcoin's transaction cost matters more; the next gives gold a 4.86% swing and bitcoin 0.35%.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: Figure 12's surface, scanned only from 0 to 0.0030 on both fees, slopes along the gold axis and looks flat along bitcoin. Neither percentage is readable from the surface, and the scan excludes the task's 1% and 2% fees. The two sentences contradict each other and both contradict using this surface as evidence about the official fees.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The memorandum delivers a 2% gold / 98% bitcoin allocation and a terminal $285,647 as the strategy for the trader.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: Figure 10 supports only the shape: drawn profit is highest at a small gold ratio and falls toward delta=100. The dollar amount and the two percentages are prose, from a bounded scan, not an optimum over all strategies, and the summary itself had hedged the same result. The skill may learn the memo's compression pattern but must not reproduce the allocation or the dollar figure as a finding.
